Definition: to break away (from just authority), i.e. trespass, apostatize, quarrel
BiblicalUsage: Pasha means to break away, to transgress, to rebel against just authority. Israel rebels against the house of David in 1 Kings 12:19, and Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab in 2 Kings 1:1 and 2 Kings 3:5. God says in Isaiah 1:2 that He has nourished children and they have rebelled against Him, and in 1 Kings 8:50 Solomon prays that God would forgive His people their transgressions.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rebellion is the breaking away that names every other sin, and Isaiah's charge is the plainest in the Bible: children nourished by God who turned on Him. That is why I hold that forgiveness is the only answer to rebellion, and Solomon prayed for it before the kingdom ever split.
